meaning: The trained model in control of the arm, called on every tick of the arm's clock.
The input to a policy at one instant: on the SO-101, six joint angles and one image per camera.
The output of a policy at one instant: on the SO-101, six target joint angles.
One period of the arm's clock: 33.3 ms at LeRobot's default of 30 per second.
One attempt at the task: a table with one row of observation and action per tick, plus one video per camera.
The open-source robot-learning library the arm is recorded, trained and run with.
The video compression format LeRobot writes by default.
NVIDIA's robot model, used here as the example of a large policy.
NVIDIA's inference compiler, the runtime of its benchmark figures.
LeRobot's default mode: the arm stands still each time the policy computes its next chunk.
The part of a machine a job fills first, which sets its speed while the others sit partly idle.
The share of time in which at least one kernel was executing on the GPU; it does not say how much of the GPU was used.
A model that predicts what happens next if the robot takes a given action.
A design that predicts a compact summary of the scene in place of its pixels.
Training by trial and reward.
Storing a model's numbers in fewer bits; NVIDIA's format on the Jetson AGX Thor is called mixed NVFP4.
The next several actions returned by one policy call and played tick by tick; the next chunk has to be ready before the actions in hand run out.
A LeRobot mode that starts the next policy call while the arm plays the chunk it holds; it works only while the actions in hand outlast the call.
The large pretrained body of a model; frozen means it is left unchanged while only the smaller parts built on it are trained.
A comparison of two output vectors that is 1 when they point the same way; the compiled model is expected to reach 0.999 or higher against the original.
